statement: Strand v0.1 adopts an 'instruments, not ornaments' philosophy: dark calm petrol chrome (#193F49), bright working paper (#FFFFFF), mist surround (#EDF1F2), and colour reserved strictly for semantic meaning paired with a label or shape.
why: Reserving colour for meaning and pairing it with text or shape keeps working surfaces calm and avoids relying on colour alone.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand defines darker ink variants for text legibility on light paper: Teal ink (#1B5F6B) for structure, Amber (#FFB301) for focus/pending, Green ink (#2E6E5B) for changed/verified values, Signal ink (#A35400) for external/volatile sources, and Red ink (#C12923) for errors.
why: Darker semantic inks preserve legibility while giving each status role a consistent visual identity.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Typography separates three voices — Recursive for UI (27/22/18/15.5/13.5/12.5/11 px scale), Source Serif 4 for reading prose, and Recursive Mono for formulas/source — with installed open/system fallbacks and zero external font downloads.
why: Distinct type voices aid scanning between UI chrome, narrative, and exact Excel source while working offline.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Strand fixes geometry radii (Cells 0, Chips 5, Cards 9, Panels 14), spacing steps (2, 4, 6, 10, 14, 22), and 120–160 ms settle motion that respects reduced-motion preferences.
why: Consistent radii, compact spacing, and restrained motion keep the working surface predictable and accessible.

statement: Normal steady state is silent, shown only by a quiet steady mark in the status bar; pending, stale, previous, error, missing-source, and delayed statuses appear only when relevant, and revision/snapshot prose never appears on working screens.
why: Keeping steady state quiet ensures genuine exceptions stand out immediately without visual clutter.

statement: Cells and controls distinguish Normal, Selected (pale fill), Active (dark outline + amber inner accent), Editing (caret), Point mode, Error, Spill anchor, Spill child, Stale, Pending, Negative, Conditional format, Hover (neutral surface), and Keyboard Focus (outer stroke distinct from active cell).
why: Making active cell, keyboard focus, hover, and data states visually distinct prevents ambiguity during navigation and editing.

statement: Stored workbook number formats (including red parenthesised negatives) and conditional formats are preserved as model content; UI states and theme restyling must not overwrite or confuse them with application attention colours.
why: Workbook formatting carries user-authored domain meaning that must stay faithful across themes and views.

statement: Review surfaces distinguish Model changes from Presentation changes with separate headings and concrete before/after diffs (explicitly stating when zero cells, formulas, or names change) within one consistent review pattern.
why: Users need clear visibility into whether an action mutates the Excel model or only presentation metadata before confirming.

statement: All workbook views share one consistent shell: command bands (File, Home, Insert, Formulas, Data, Review, View), command search (Alt+Q), source address box, formula bar, view picker, sheet tabs, zoom control, and status bar.
why: A shared shell preserves orientation, source visibility, and workbook navigation across every view.

statement: Every view inside an open workbook shares one model state, one selection, one clock (when present), and one Undo history; switching views changes presentation only and never copies values or creates a second model.
why: Eliminating duplicated state ensures edits, repairs, and Undo behave consistently across views.
evidence: README.md, W04, NC07, S08, S09, F02

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified ¶3; verification.html §What was checked ¶5
statement: All UI iconography and assets are self-contained original SVGs with zero CDN calls, external web-font downloads, or Microsoft artwork/styling.
why: Guarantees offline reliability, zero external network dependencies, and copyright cleanliness.

statement: Every screen supports 200% zoom reflow (stacking split panes vertically when needed), high-contrast mode, reduced-motion mode, labelled form controls, and visible two-stroke keyboard focus on buttons, fields, and ports.
why: Ensures accessibility is designed and inspectable across every view and exception variant.

statement: Every scene pairs a Normal/story state with an Exception variant and three to six callouts in a 1440×900 product frame, with Previous/Next arrow stepping disabled when focus is inside an interactive control.
why: Designing normal and exception states at equal fidelity prevents error and refusal paths from being an afterthought.

statement: In the computation notebook, every written Excel formula sits directly above its live evaluated output, followed by the next formula and result with prose between links; this vertical chain is the primary reading surface.
why: Showing written formula above live output delivers a Jupyter-like computation chain without hiding the Excel source.
evidence: NC01–NC07; Sales Analysis!A10# → J10# → M10# → Q10# → U10# → J2

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (callout 1), NC07 (callout 2, 3); verification.html §A function cell ¶4
statement: Author, Read, and Across are presentations of the exact same underlying cells and workbook names; switching layouts changes presentation only without copying values or creating scenarios, and Read layout still shows every formula above its output.
why: Separating layout from calculation prevents authoring and reading views from drifting out of sync.

statement: Data-frame outputs show a compact row preview window (e.g., 4 or 10 rows) while explicitly displaying full dimensions and evaluating FILTER, GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, SORTBY, and totals across all 25,000 source rows; paging the window never alters aggregates.
why: Prevents a compact display window from being mistaken for a sampled calculation.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01, NC06 (callout 4, UI); verification.html §The computation lives in cells and names ¶2
statement: The notebook's visible backing sheet (Sales!Analysis) puts inputs in B2:B6, scalars above row 10 (J2, J5), notes in column Y (Y10), and dynamic-array spills in separate column lanes starting at row 10 (A:G, J:K, M:N, Q:R, U:V) so downward spills do not collide.
why: Separate column lanes allow vertical notebook reading order while giving every Excel dynamic array room to grow downward.
evidence: NC01, NC06, verification.html; A10:G…, J10:K…, M10:N…, Q10:R…, U10:V…

statement: Each notebook output binds to a workbook defined name (e.g., =Analysis!$A$10#); clicking an output name allows renaming with workbook-name syntax validation, conflict rejection, and exact updates to downstream references while keeping the cell anchor fixed.
why: Keeps formulas readable by name while maintaining standard Excel worksheet anchors.
evidence: NC01, NC02; scopeOrders, byRegion, byMonth, rankedOrders, chartData, scopeTotal

statement: Clicking a workbook name inside a later formula or live prose navigates directly to its producing cell in the computation chain.
why: Lets readers trace dependencies through the notebook in one click.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (callout 3, UI); verification.html §A function cell ¶5
statement: PIVOTBY in the computation notebook produces a dynamic-array formula result (using explicit header/total arguments and keeping its month-heading row in the backing spill) rather than a PivotTable cache, and never invents extra months beyond source data.
why: Clarifies exact Excel PIVOTBY semantics and backing spill dimensions (e.g., 3×2 spill for 2 regions × 1 month 2026-11).

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (UI); verification.html §A chart has ordinary data sources
statement: Notebook charts are ordinary Excel chart objects (SalesByRegion) referencing dynamic workbook names (Chart.Region and Chart.Amount via INDEX+ROWS over the ranked spill) rather than an invented worksheet chart function.
why: Ensures charts remain standard native objects when opened in Excel.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC02 (callouts 2, 4, UI); verification.html §A function cell ¶4
statement: Editing a notebook formula inline offers Ctrl+Space completion and signature help (`FILTER(array, include, [if_empty])`), and complete supported expressions recalculate immediately with no Run button required.
why: Matches Excel's live recalculation model inside a notebook editor.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC02 (callouts 2, 4, exception); README.md §Computation notebook route ¶2
statement: An incomplete or unsupported formula draft replaces all dependent notebook displays with an explicit draft state so stale outputs never masquerade as current successes; Escape restores the committed expression.
why: Prevents misleading stale results from sitting underneath an unparseable or half-edited formula.

statement: Notebook filter controls (Region, Status, inclusive November date handles clamped to valid dates) bind directly to ordinary cells (Analysis!B2:B5); changes update all downstream tables, charts, and prose immediately with brief change marks and no Run button.
why: Keeps interactive parameter controls backed by standard Excel cells.
evidence: NC03; Paid = 20,853 rows / R23,440,150; South > East by R25

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC01 (exception), NC03 (callout 4, exception), NC07 (exception); verification.html §Spill growth ¶2
statement: Omitting if_empty on FILTER produces Excel's #CALC! when zero rows match, and downstream cells use explicit IF(ISERROR($A$10),$A$10,...) guards to forward the error cleanly with no earlier successful outputs or chart remaining.
why: Maintains exact Excel error propagation and avoids leaving stale visuals next to an errored filter.
evidence: NC01, NC03, NC07 exception variants; verification.html [T10]

statement: A LET formula cell expands an inline live binding tree showing formula structure and current evaluated values of each binding (items, amounts, SUM(amounts)), explicitly labelled as expression structure rather than a runtime execution trace.
why: Makes nested LET formulas inspectable in place without claiming to record Excel's firing order.

statement: Live RTD cells in the notebook (`Report!E2 =RTD("DnaCalc.Price",,"LARK","last")` feeding `Analysis!J5`) share one stream with Inspector (I02) and Data frame (N01), clean up old observers on navigation, and reveal Report!E2 accurately.
why: Prevents duplicate or leaked RTD observers across views of the same workbook.

statement: Generating gallery previews or print snapshots must be pure and never consume or advance a live RTD price observation or clock tick.
why: Prevents passive UI rendering or printing from mutating live stream state.

statement: When a live RTD provider is unavailable, the notebook asserts no current price or dependent valuation while keeping historical order totals completely independent and unaffected.
why: Isolates live feed outages from historical workbook calculations and prevents stale valuations from appearing live.

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC05 (callouts 2, 3, 4, UI, exception); verification.html §A function cell
statement: A notebook function cell defines a workbook-scoped defined name referring to a LAMBDA (`MarginPct =LAMBDA(revenue,cost,IF(revenue=0,0,(revenue-cost)/revenue))`) whose output displays a callable signature rather than a fabricated scalar from an uncalled worksheet cell, invoked by ordinary callers across any sheet.
why: Matches Excel's named-LAMBDA contract so reusable notebook functions work natively in Excel.

statement: Dynamic-array spill growth is a real model event: when a growing FILTER hits an obstructing formula cell (A16), A10 returns #SPILL! and explicit error guards forward #SPILL! to all dependents with zero partial output, prior chart, or successful-looking prose remaining.
why: Makes Excel's spill collision semantics honest and unmistakable in the notebook.
evidence: NC06; West+Pending A10:G10 vs All A10:G4156 blocked at A16

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC06 (callout 3, UI, exception); verification.html §Spill growth ¶2
statement: Reviewing a spill relocation moves only the obstructing formula and its defined name (e.g., reviewNote `="Review with Sam"`) to an empty cell (Y10 or Y12) without altering FILTER; Apply is disabled if the proposed destination is occupied, Cancel is inert, and Undo restores A16 and the #SPILL! blockage.
why: Repairs spill conflicts safely without overwriting user cells or altering the growing formula.
evidence: NC06; A16 → Y10 (or Y12 when Y10 occupied)

source: pro21/notebook-compute.html NC06 (callout 5, UI), NC01; verification.html §Corrections table row 3
statement: Opening Classic / Backing cells from the computation notebook shows the exact current live calculation state (preserving active criteria like Paid) with outlined worksheet anchors mapped directly to the adjacent notebook cells.
why: Demonstrates that the notebook and Classic grid are two views of the exact same live cells.

source: pro21/verification.html §The computation lives in cells and names ¶1
statement: Date values in proposed Analysis workbooks must be stored as real Excel date serial numbers in native files; ISO date strings are only an HTML prototype representation.
why: Ensures DATE() filter comparisons evaluate accurately in native Excel.

statement: The Sales computation notebook backs its chain with concrete Excel formulas using structured Table references, FILTER, IF(ISERROR(...)) guards, GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, SORTBY, LET, and RTD, preserving accepted user-edited formula text as written.
why: Grounds the computation notebook in exact verifiable Excel syntax rather than pseudo-code.

statement: Starting an empty Notebook while a cell is selected (e.g., Summary!B7) offers a concrete first step ('Add selected result') so authors build narratives directly around live workbook results.
why: Removes blank-page friction and anchors new notebooks to real worksheet cells from the start.

source: pro21/notebook.html F03 (callouts 1, 2, 4, UI, exception); storyboards.html S04 (callouts 1, 2, UI)
statement: A director-review Notebook embeds bound live numbers in narrative prose, workbook-owned charts, and cell-bound controls (slider, dropdown, Boolean checkbox), explicitly noting when an input (e.g., Debtor days Inputs!B12) does not affect an excerpt and keeping sibling valid cards visible when one card hits #SPILL!.
why: Combines executive narrative with live model exploration without detaching figures from their cells.
evidence: F03, S04; Budget Inputs!B3, B12, Summary!D2, B7, A20

source: pro21/notebook.html F03 (callout 3, UI); storyboards.html S05 (callout 3, UI)
statement: The Formula lens is a read-only presentation showing human-readable terms alongside the exact source formula (e.g., Revenue − Variable cost − Fixed cost beside =B8-B9-B10) without rewriting the source formula or adding workbook names.
why: Aids formula comprehension without silently mutating the underlying spreadsheet.

statement: Sorting or filtering a Notebook data frame over an Excel Table defaults to View-only presentation and leaves the Table's stored filter and row addresses untouched.
why: Prevents casual exploration from accidentally mutating shared Excel Tables.

statement: Choosing 'Changes the Table' on a Notebook data frame goes through explicit review and Apply to sort/filter the shared Table and update sheet row addresses (with Undo restoring row order and stored filters), while Find and Copy all matches always operate on the full matching scope.
why: Supports deliberate Table mutations with clear review and Undo alongside complete-scope search/copy.

statement: A live RTD price embedded in Notebook prose stays separate from historical Table rows, labels its last received value as 'stale' when the source is unavailable, and never revises historical order amounts.
why: Keeps live external feed staleness visible and isolated from immutable historical records.

statement: The horizontal Notebook pipeline lays out existing sheets left-to-right (Inputs → Monthly → Summary) as reading order without altering calculation order, labels windowed excerpts (3 of 12 months while the annual total sums all 12), and marks prior result cards 'Previous result' while an input change is pending.
why: Offers a cross-sheet flow overview while staying honest about calculation order, excerpt windows, and pending recalculation.

source: pro21/classic.html F01 (callouts 1, 2, 3, 4, UI, exception), C02 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI, exception)
statement: In Classic formula editing and Point mode, switching sheets to pick references keeps the original edit destination fixed (e.g., editing Monthly!B8 while picking Inputs!B3); references use coloured, numbered tokens and distinct border patterns, pending drafts never overwrite committed values, and Enter/Commit vs Escape preserve distinct commit/cancel semantics.
why: Matches Excel's cross-sheet reference picking while making references accessible without relying on colour alone.

statement: Pressing Alt displays discoverable key tips over compact original command controls (borrowing Excel's command access structure without copying Microsoft artwork), Escape dismisses key tips, and every command remains available via Alt+Q search.
why: Supports rapid keyboard-driven command invocation familiar to Excel users.

statement: F4 (and four matching anchor buttons) cycles a formula reference through relative, fully absolute, row-absolute, and column-absolute forms (B3 → $B$3 → B$3 → $B3), showing that anchoring changes copy adjustment without altering the current source value.
why: Delivers exact Excel F4 muscle memory with clear feedback.

statement: Dragging the fill handle shows a destination hatch and live preview of the adjusted destination formula (`=F8-F9-F10`), applies normal relative-reference copying on release, offers a visible Fill button alternative, and reverses in one Undo step.
why: Pairs familiar Excel fill gestures with live formula previews and keyboard/click accessibility.

statement: Ctrl+Enter writes one entry into all cells of a multi-cell selection while retaining the selection, offers a visible button alternative, reverses in one Undo step, and is never intercepted by shell or agent shortcuts.
why: Protects core Excel multi-cell entry muscle memory from shell or AI shortcut collisions.

statement: Dragging a cell's border previews the destination outline and moves the cell intact (e.g., Summary!A21 → D21 to unblock `=TRANSPOSE(Monthly!B11:M11)` at A20), Undo restores both the cell and `#SPILL!`, and spill children cannot be edited independently.
why: Supports standard Excel border-drag moves and lossless spill recovery.

statement: Alt+Q opens keyboard-navigable command search (filter, Up/Down, Enter, Escape returning focus to the active cell) inside dense workbooks, keeping missing external sources (Rates2024.xlsx) and disabled macros (LegacyClose) clearly separated from the selected local formula.
why: Lets analysts find and run commands without losing coordinate focus in dense spreadsheets.

statement: Opening a large workbook displays the last saved viewport immediately with stale values visibly labelled (never silently refreshing missing links), runs background reference inspection (e.g., 12/40 sheets) without blocking navigation, editing, or inspection, lists visible/hidden sheet counts in the outline, and surfaces recovery state.
why: Keeps large workbooks immediately usable on open while staying strictly honest about saved vs recalculated values.

statement: Classic verification preserves live model state from Model map (including unapplied repairs), supports native cell-bound form-control sliders (Stock!B5), shows explicit iteration settings (max 100, tolerance 0.001) without inventing an iteration count, and on a non-converging proposal (`B8=B8+1`) retains the current reserve without claiming an observed iteration stop.
why: Keeps grid verification synchronised with Model map and honest about iterative calculation limits.

statement: Ctrl+Z in a source view dispatches the actual owning model's Undo stack, while text input fields retain standard native text-editing keys.
why: Prevents Undo shortcuts from hitting the wrong owner or breaking standard text editing.

source: pro21/inspector.html F02 (callouts 1, 2, UI, exception); storyboards.html S06 (callouts 1, 2, UI)
statement: Inspector diagnoses valid-Excel-but-wrong-business-answer results by tracing full-scope contributions across all 25,000 rows and isolating specific outlier rows with both Table data row and worksheet row addresses.
why: Helps users uncover semantic spreadsheet errors that produce ordinary numbers instead of Excel error codes.
evidence: F02, S06; Sales Report!B5 128,450 vs 124,250; SO10482 data row 10482 / Orders!A10483:G10483

statement: When a PivotTable cross-check has an unrefreshed cache, Inspector labels it 'Stale cache' and refuses to treat its previous total as current confirmation until refreshed.
why: Prevents stale PivotTable caches from giving false confirmation during auditing.
evidence: S06, S07 exception variants; Pivot previous 124,250

statement: Inspecting a proposed one-formula repair previews exact before/after formula text, result delta, and changed-formula count separately from the current result until Apply; Undo restores the original formula, Cancel discards only a pending preview, and Close retains an accepted change.
why: Makes diagnostic repairs exact, reviewable, and cleanly reversible.
evidence: F02, S06, S07; Report!B5 adding Orders[Status],"Paid" (diff −4,200)

statement: Inspector traces a local #REF! directly to a broken defined-name formula (`Revenue.Window =OFFSET(Revenue!#REF!,0,0,12,1)`) separately from unrelated missing external workbooks, never presents stale cached values as the current formula result, and never guesses a replacement reference.
why: Isolates local name errors from external-link noise and prevents guesswork repairs.
evidence: S02; Inherited Summary!F18, cached 2,401,300 vs #REF!, Rates2024.xlsx

statement: Inspector's Copy evidence action preserves formula, name scope, error origin, and the stale-vs-current distinction, Reveal in Classic carries the exact selection across views, and protected sheets still allow inspection while requiring an authorised editable copy before repair.
why: Produces auditable diagnostic handoffs and respects worksheet protection without hiding evidence.

source: pro21/inspector.html F02 (callout 3), I01–I03 (callout 4); storyboards.html S02 (callout 2); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶5
statement: Dependency graphs, highlights, and wire animations are strictly dependency explanations and are never presented as recordings of Excel's execution order; any optional recorded order must be labelled 'DNA Calc's calculation order' and never invented.
why: Excel's dynamic calculation chain is implementation-defined, so claiming a dependency picture shows Excel's execution order is inaccurate.
evidence: F02, I01–I03, S02, F04, M02, O04, D03, verification.html

source: pro21/inspector.html I01 (callout 1, UI, exception), I02 (callout 1), I03 (callout 1)
statement: Live instruments keep observation capture controls (Record, Pause capture, Clear) strictly separate from the source's own Run/Pause controls; pausing capture leaves the source running and labels the chart as a recorded observation rather than a live result.
why: Lets analysts freeze and inspect recordings without interrupting or altering the live data source.

source: pro21/inspector.html I01 (callout 2, UI), I02 (callout 2), I03 (callout 2, UI)
statement: Minimum, maximum, and last statistics are computed strictly from the displayed observation recording, and Replay scrubs a cursor through recorded observations without writing to workbook inputs or replaying RTD events into the workbook.
why: Guarantees post-hoc analysis of recorded runs is side-effect-free.

statement: The RTD price instrument separately discloses source update rate, observation sampling rate, session received count, observed count, coalesced count, and last-received age (keeping the latest update per interval without claiming lossless capture), and retains the last received price labelled 'stale' with age when disconnected.
why: Prevents throttled or disconnected real-time feeds from appearing complete or falsely live.

source: pro21/inspector.html I03 (UI, exception); verification.html §What the controls mean ¶2
statement: In the ticked Live panel, Reset explicitly restores tick 0, stock 400, and an empty pipeline without erasing an existing observation recording (Clear is a separate action), and missing clock/guard evidence classifies self-referencing cells as Unknown.
why: Prevents simulation resets from accidentally wiping diagnostic recordings while enforcing honest cycle classification.

statement: Inspector organizes tools into four tabs — Precedents, Dependents, Calculation, and Live — alongside pinned signals, recorded runs, Copy evidence, and one-step Source navigation.
why: Groups diagnostic evidence and live instrumentation cleanly while keeping backing cells one step away.

source: pro21/model-map.html F04 (callout 3, exception), M01 (callout 3, exception), M02 (callout 3); S08 (callout 3); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶5
statement: Model map uses distinct visual structures and labels to separate period-row delays (`H15→C18`), per-tick state delays (`z⁻¹`), and within-calculation iterative circular references (Reserve enclosure); a circular reference without confirmed delay or iteration settings is labelled Unknown rather than inventing a mechanism.
why: A circular reference is not a delay; conflating period lags, clocked state, and iterative solving misrepresents model semantics.
evidence: F04, M01, M02, S08, D03, O04, verification.html

source: pro21/model-map.html F04 (callouts 1, 2, 4, UI), M01 (callouts 1, 4, UI), D03 (callout 3)
statement: Map nodes display live values on source-bound ports, support keyboard selection, provide a Source toggle for compact inline formulas and a grid button for backing cells, and expose a Connections list as a keyboard- and reduced-motion-accessible alternative to thin animated wires.
why: Keeps diagrams anchored to exact cells while ensuring full accessibility without mouse hovering or animation.

statement: Hierarchical map groups (e.g., Replenishment) open into member nodes and return through breadcrumbs (`Stock › Replenishment › Day 5`) without losing selection or shared parameter controls.
why: Supports layered systems-model navigation without duplicating sheets.

statement: Wiring a port to a specific operand on the Model map previews the exact before/after Excel formula and current-vs-preview value before Apply (leaving other order formulas intact); subsequent parameter edits recompute both sides of the preview, Cancel closes pending preview, Close keeps accepted changes, and protected targets permit preview inspection while blocking Apply.
why: Maps graphical wiring strictly onto reviewable, cell-specific Excel formula edits.

source: pro21/model-map.html M02 (callouts 1, 4, UI); app.html A02 (callouts 1, 2); verification.html §The ticked model's explicit contract
statement: The ticked Stock demonstration advances day, stock, and a 3-stage pipeline exactly once per accepted RTD clock tick from one immutable previous-tick snapshot (`Prev.*`), with reorder-point edits acting prospectively (keeping orders already in pipeline) and pre-order position (200) labelled separately from post-order stock+pipeline (620).
why: Defines an unambiguous discrete-time state transition and keeps decision-time position distinct from post-order inventory.
evidence: M02, A02, I03, verification.html; tick 0–5 table at reorder 260 and 320

source: pro21/model-map.html M02 (callout 2, exception); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶1–2
statement: An RTD topic, MaxIterations=1, and a self-reference pattern suggest a candidate clocked model but do NOT by themselves prove an immutable previous-state snapshot, once-only tick consumption, or delivery of every server event in Excel (whose RTD.ThrottleInterval defaults to 2000 ms and which recalculates on edits and async completions); a production host/provider profile must establish those guarantees and handle missing or repeated tick IDs.
why: Maintains strict honesty against Microsoft Excel's documented RTD and recalculation mechanics.
evidence: M02, A02, I03, verification.html [T1–T3, T6, T8–T9]

source: pro21/model-map.html M02 (callouts 3, 6); app.html A02 (callout 3); inspector.html I03 (callout 6); verification.html §Why the file alone ¶3–4
statement: Because Excel exposes Application.MaxIterations at Application scope, the 100-iteration period scene and 1-iteration ticked scene are alternative calculation profiles rather than simultaneous per-sheet iteration limits; the ticked reserve starts at its fixed point 20 and does not claim an independent 100-iteration solver.
why: Prevents the design from claiming per-sheet iteration limits that Excel does not support.

source: pro21/model-map.html M02 (exception); app.html A02 (callout 5, exception); inspector.html I03 (callout 5, exception)
statement: Whenever file evidence is insufficient to confirm the guarded per-tick clock contract, the UI labels the circular relationship 'Unknown', refuses to start the assumed clock contract, and offers source inspection.
why: Refuses to animate or execute an unverified cycle interpretation.

statement: For large workbooks (e.g., 40 sheets, 300,000 formula members, 90 directed links, 85,272 reference records), Model map enforces a proposed 200-node / 400-edge viewport display budget, drawing counted sheet groups initially (8 shown, 32 collapsed in a searchable inventory) and refusing 'Expand all cells' in favour of blocks or a counted reference list without losing selection or deleting data.
why: Keeps Model map legible and bounded at enterprise scale instead of rendering an unreadable graph.

statement: Map grouping and expansion change presentation only (creating 0 formulas, names, or calculation scopes) and preserve hidden-sheet visibility; when dependency analysis has partial scope (e.g., 18/40 sheets resolved), unresolved boundaries stay explicitly visible without treating them as missing data.
why: Ensures scaling abstractions never mutate the workbook or hide incomplete analysis.

statement: Opening a large sheet group decomposes it into explicit contiguous calculation blocks (e.g., Revenue B4:M4003 into four 1,000-row × 12-column blocks of 12,000 formulas each) while keeping every declared formula exception (D63, H219, F2058) explicitly visible and separating missing external links (Rates2024.xlsx) from local block membership.
why: Compresses repetitive formula regions without hiding rare formula overrides or misrepresenting external links.

statement: Model map supports an optional bounded geometry-preserving sheet excerpt inside the map (7 of 1,000 rows × 12 columns) displaying exact addresses, formulas, and full-precision values alongside surrounding blocks and boundary ports; paging/hiding is presentation only, and a changed-binding fingerprint exception requires explicit current-block confirmation rather than silently substituting another range.
why: Lets analysts inspect exact cell geometry inside the map without switching away or trusting stale bindings.

source: pro21/app.html F05 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI), S10 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI), A03 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI)
statement: App view defaults to live inputs: focusing an input reveals 'Model change' and the bound source cell before typing, valid edits immediately recalculate outputs, charts (from all active amortisation rows), and schedule (full precision internally, display-rounded currency, unrounded residual inspectable), Undo reverses each gesture, and Compare shows the last applied case.
why: Delivers an immediate form experience backed directly by Excel formulas with transparent source binding.

source: pro21/app.html A03 (callouts 2, 4, UI), F05 (exception), S10 (exception), A01 (callout 3, exception)
statement: App inputs enforce workbook Stop validation (principal > 0, annual rate 0–100%, integer term 1–360); invalid entries stay visible as inline drafts, write nothing to the model, and leave the last valid results explicitly labelled 'Previous valid inputs'.
why: Protects the workbook from invalid entries and prevents stale outputs from looking valid for the draft.

statement: Batched input is a named author-chosen option (with its reason displayed beside the controls) rather than the default: unapplied deltas cannot relabel applied results ('Previous valid inputs'), Apply commits all valid edits atomically as one Undo step, Discard restores displayed values, Escape cancels only the focused field, and switching back to Live is explicit and discards unapplied drafts.
why: Supports deliberate multi-parameter review without imposing Apply-button friction on ordinary live Apps.

statement: App print preview captures a frozen print snapshot of the applied case (snapshot ID in footer only, never on the working App), defaults to a 1-page summary with full-precision balance chart, and optionally appends the full 360-row schedule (1 summary + 10 pages × 36 rows) with visible page-count updates.
why: Produces clean, traceable stakeholder reports directly from the live workbook.
evidence: S11; Loan.xlsx print snapshot L1, 1 page vs 11 pages

statement: The ticked operating App panel shares Run, Pause, Step, Rate, Reorder point, Stop condition (tick limit or stock=0), and Reset controls with Model map and Inspector, plots only observed ticks, shows the 3-stage delivery pipeline, and pauses at configured boundaries requiring explicit Reset so the recorded run is not silently discarded.
why: Gives operators a clean simulation console synchronized with Model map and Inspector.
evidence: A02; Stock (ticked) tick 0–30, stock 400, pipeline Due in 1/2/3 ticks

statement: Docked Formula Explorer opens with a real caller cell (`Summary!D14`) and evaluates trial formulas, argument edits, formats, and rules in isolation without mutating the source cell; Apply writes one formula edit with one shared Undo step, with Ctrl+Enter to evaluate, F6 to cycle regions, and Ctrl+Z to undo.
why: Allows safe formula experimentation in real workbook context before committing changes.

source: pro21/formula-explorer.html F07 (callout 1, UI), S13 (callout 1, UI), E01 (callouts 1, 4, UI, exception)
statement: Standalone Formula Explorer (skin 0) has no workbook, sheet tabs, caller cell, or hidden temporary workbook and accepts literal arguments only; context- or caller-dependent functions (`DNA.CALLERADDRESS()`, `DNA.CallerRow()`, `WEBSERVICE`) are refused explicitly as a tool/host state rather than disguised as a cell error, preserving the draft and offering to open in DNA Calc.
why: Keeps skin-0 layering strictly honest without faking a hidden workbook or cell errors.

statement: Formula Explorer supports saving, loading, editing (with Undo), and running expected-value test cases; an expected Excel error (`#NUM!` for rate 1.2) evaluates as a passing 'Match' while keeping the `#NUM!` error visibly displayed.
why: Supports test-driven formula verification including negative/error cases without hiding errors.

source: pro21/formula-explorer.html E01 (callouts 1, 2, 3, 4, UI); verification.html §What was checked list 3
statement: The Formula Explorer function browser provides search, family filters, signatures, argument help, runnable examples, host-availability tags, an inline live LET tree, and per-function Excel-match/worst-ULP records clearly labelled as sample archive evidence rather than unmeasured claims; malformed or unsupported expressions are rejected while preserving drafts.
why: Combines function discovery, compatibility evidence, and live expression inspection in one workbench.
evidence: E01; GAMMA 4,252/4,311 · 63 ulp worst; PMT 128/128 · 0 ulp; LET live tree

statement: The Formatting playground evaluates an array formula (`=SEQUENCE(6,3,-1250,250)`) and displays raw numeric values beside formatted text under selectable format codes and display locales (`en-US`, `en-ZA`, `fr-FR`, `de-DE`), evaluating conditional-format rules against the underlying numbers BEFORE text formatting with hatch + text labels as well as colour; unsupported format drafts are rejected without replacing the applied format, and formatting edits have Undo.
why: Demonstrates the separation between stored values, locale formatting, and numeric conditional-format evaluation.

source: pro21/formula-explorer.html E03 (callouts 1, 2, 3, UI, exception), F06 (callout 4, exception), F07 (callout 4, exception), S12 (exception), S13 (exception)
statement: The Add-in library inspects loaded providers (`.xll`, `.xlam`), versions, categories, argument metadata, and host capability limits; unloading a provider or lacking its desktop execution host refuses execution while retaining the formula draft and any cached source result without silently substituting an execution route.
why: Keeps add-in provenance visible and prevents silent fallback or draft loss when providers are missing.
evidence: E03, F06, F07, S12, S13; DiscountFunctions.xll 1.0, AnalysisTools.xlam

statement: Native XLL code is explicitly NOT contained by the VBA Guarded policy; any real desktop XLL provider requires an independently selected execution host and trust policy.
why: Prevents users from falsely assuming VBA macro guardrails sandbox native binary XLL add-ins.

statement: Pattern recognition separates workbook facts from author interpretations using exactly four labels — From workbook, Suggested, Confirmed by Maria, Needs review after change — with zero invented confidence percentages; confirmation and correction write presentation metadata only (0 values, formulas, names, Tables, or sheet visibility changed).
why: Keeps structural interpretation transparent and non-destructive instead of using opaque confidence scores.

statement: Workbook Structure summarises sheet counts, formula counts, hidden sheets, and recognised patterns (inputs, repeated blocks, time series, director report, sheet pipeline, repeated sheet family, external rates, unclassified form) before opening thousands of cells; listing hidden sheets never reveals their cells or changes visibility, and partial dependency resolution (18/40 sheets) keeps the full sheet inventory available.
why: Provides a safe high-level map of unfamiliar workbooks while respecting hidden sheets and partial analysis.
evidence: W01; Inherited-structure-v1 40 sheets, 6 hidden, 300,000 formulas, 8 patterns

statement: Suggested patterns show concrete evidence (12 real dates in row 1, 48 repeated formulas in B8:M11, 0 overrides) while noting repetition alone does not prove chronological order or certify formulas; confirming records range, heading row, order, interpretation, author name, and evidence fingerprint, later header/range/exception edits flip state to 'Needs review after change' without invalidating the workbook, correcting lets the user reclassify, and confirming a mixed date/caption axis requires explicit caption review.
why: Makes pattern confirmations auditable and self-invalidating when worksheets change.
evidence: W02; Budget Monthly!B1:M11; exception H1 → 'Jul actuals'

statement: Declared Excel Tables (`Orders!A1:G25001`) are recognised as 'From workbook' database structure without silently converting ordinary ranges; full-scope key checks (25,000 distinct OrderIDs, 0 duplicates) support display-key confirmation, resolved consumers track current post-sort addresses, and unresolved dynamic references (`Report!H2 =INDIRECT(B9)`) remain explicitly separate and uncounted.
why: Grounds sheet-as-database views in real Excel Table declarations and honest dependency resolution.
evidence: W03; Orders 25,000 rows, Report!B5, Report!A12, exception Report!H2

statement: One workbook supports a distinct preferred view per sheet (e.g., Inputs Classic, Monthly Model map, Summary Notebook), with each sheet tab naming its view; switching tabs restores sheet source and presentation without copying formulas, a local view selector creates a session override separate from file defaults, and a missing layout falls back to Classic at the exact selected source while preserving the unresolved preference without substituting a neighbouring layout.
why: Allows heterogeneous sheet views inside one workbook with Classic guaranteed as a lossless fallback.
evidence: W04; Budget Inputs (Classic), Monthly (Model map), Summary (Notebook, Summary!B7)

source: pro21/workbook.html W05 (callouts 1, 2, UI), O02 (callouts 1, 2, UI); verification.html §A chart ¶2
statement: View preferences, supported views, per-sheet layouts, confirmed interpretations, and notebook prose travel in an optional versioned custom-XML part (proposed namespace `urn:dnacalc:views:v1`, version `1`, with a production writer allocating a free part name rather than colliding on `/customXml/item1.xml`) using stable sheet IDs, layout IDs, and source bindings, committed via Review/Apply.
why: Stores rich DNA Calc view metadata cleanly inside standard .xlsx/.xlsm files without altering Excel model parts.

statement: Classic is always available as the ordinary-reader fallback, explicit reader choices take precedence over saved file defaults, and unsupported future view-part versions (e.g., version 3) are retained opaquely and refused overwrite by older editors.
why: Guarantees forward/backward safety and ensures workbooks remain readable in Excel and across DNA Calc versions.

source: pro21/workbook.html O02 (callouts 3, 4, UI, exception); verification.html §Corrections table row 4
statement: File Save quietly notes that views travel with the workbook beside a three-part breakdown (Excel model, DNA Calc views, Ordinary-reader fallback) and offers separate JSON export of view settings; legacy `.xls` (unable to carry custom-XML) and macro-losing `.xlsx` save choices are refused in both UI and handlers rather than silently dropping presentation or code.
why: Prevents silent loss of macros or view declarations when choosing incompatible save formats.

source: pro21/workbook.html O01 (callouts 1, 2, 3, 4, UI, exception); verification.html §Corrections table row 5
statement: File Open shows recent workbooks with preferred view and Classic fallback, offers 'New from a pattern' disclosing ordinary sheets/cells/linked formulas before creation (with scoped Undo that preserves other books and refuses to overwrite later edits), and handles unavailable locations without substituting an empty workbook or erasing files.
why: Makes workbook creation transparent about real Excel structure and safe against missing paths or overbroad Undo.

source: pro21/workbook.html O03 (callouts 1, 2, 3, 4, UI, exception), O04 (callout 4, UI)
statement: Print previews capture a frozen snapshot from the current shared model that never silently changes until explicit Refresh, record snapshot identifiers only in print footers, apply/clean up page orientation, and withhold successful-looking values whenever source calculations are blocked or errored.
why: Prevents printed pages from silently mutating or printing stale values over a broken model.
evidence: O03 (Sales snapshot N1), O04 (Stock snapshot M1), NC07

statement: Notebook print uses A4 portrait to present the current computation chain as a clean write-up (with live-price outputs explicitly marked as captured/non-updating) and offers an optional formula appendix listing exact formulas and backing anchors that visibly updates page count.
why: Produces clean stakeholder write-ups with optional full formula auditability.

statement: Model map print uses A4 landscape for a readable selected region (e.g., 5 blocks with optional backing-formula appendix) preserving period-delay vs iteration distinctions and dependency-explanation disclaimers, and refuses automatic unreadable expansion when a larger scope exceeds one page.
why: Ensures printed model maps stay readable and semantically faithful on paper.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Customisation Studio edits an inspectable declarative manifest (`dna.view/1` JSON covering view, density, formula size, inspector dock/width, reading order, and source bindings); 'Try in this window' previews purely with 0 model writes, Review lists exact presentation diffs, Apply commits one session presentation unit with Undo, and 200% zoom reflows editor and preview vertically.
why: Makes layout customisation declarative, inspectable, reversible, and strictly isolated from workbook calculations.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Applying a view declaration requires valid JSON, geometry constraints, and BOTH stable identity and exact source address to match; broken bindings block Apply and never silently fall back to a nearby cell.
why: Prevents drifted layout bindings from silently reading or writing the wrong worksheet cell.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Theme editing computes unrounded sRGB relative-luminance contrast across nine declared semantic pairs (≥ 4.5:1 for text, ≥ 3:1 for control boundaries and visible focus strokes); failing pairs block Review/Apply until corrected or reset, error/verified/external roles stay distinct, focus uses two strokes (amber inside, dark outside), and themes cannot alter workbook formats, calculation, or macro permissions.
why: Replaces subjective theming with objective contrast enforcement while bounding themes strictly to presentation.
evidence: U02; 9/9 pass vs exception secondary text 2.01:1 fail

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Remapping a reviewable Ready-grid command (e.g., Edit cell `F2 → Ctrl+Shift+E`) explicitly flags departure from the Classic conformance profile while keeping formula-editing F2/F4 contexts intact, and offers one-step 'Restore Classic' with presentation Apply and Undo.
why: Allows custom keybindings while keeping Excel-Classic conformance explicit and easily recoverable.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Core commands (`Escape`, `Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y`, `F4`, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Alt+Q`) are protected from reassignment, draft collisions (e.g., `Ctrl+E` Flash Fill) block Apply, and installation still requires a host/browser-wide conflict check beyond the declared command set.
why: Protects essential editing invariants and alerts users to shortcut conflicts.
evidence: U03 exception; Ctrl+E Flash Fill collision

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: The Keymap editor includes an isolated single-cell trial bench to test the draft chord (`Esc` cancels without writing to the workbook) before applying the profile to the live Classic source editor.
why: Lets users verify new keybindings safely before committing them.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: An agent restyling proposal (e.g., dark Classic preserving Working density, 15.5 px formula text, and 320 px right Inspector) is judged against Strand checklists (density, type step, visible source/error text, unchanged keymap/bindings, 0 model writes, 9/9 sRGB contrast checks with amber inner focus stroke on dark paper) and uses the same preview, Review, Apply, and Undo workflow without altering stored workbook formatting.
why: Holds agent-generated presentation changes to the same declarative review and measurable Strand checks as human edits.
evidence: U04; dark secondary ink #A4B8C2 on #22343C (6.29:1) vs failing #7D97A0 (4.19:1)

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: From a short user prompt, an agent proposes a bound App layout disclosing exact Read/Write source bindings, explicit tab order, and reused workbook Stop validation, without ever supplying a second calculation formula.
why: Enables rapid agent-assisted App authoring while preserving single-evaluator and explicit write-scope guarantees.
evidence: U05; Loan!B2:B4 Write, B6:B7 Read, loan.balanceChart, A12:F371

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Trial inputs in an App proposal run strictly in isolation; accepting the App layout stores presentation only and never writes trial values into the workbook, after which the accepted App edits live inputs with one Undo per committed edit.
why: Prevents exploratory trial numbers from leaking into real workbook cells upon layout acceptance.
evidence: U05; trial 12% → R10,286.13 isolated from source

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: When a proposed App binding points to an invalid address (e.g., Loan!B8 instead of Loan!B6), output and chart previews are withheld and Apply is blocked with zero approximate-cell fallback or hidden permission grants.
why: Enforces strict binding integrity in agent-generated Apps.
evidence: U05 exception; unresolved payment binding B8

statement: Agent workbook proposals split into discrete labelled units distinguishing requested model edits, presentation edits, and explicitly flagged unsupported agent suggestions; ticking unit checkboxes is completely inert until Review and Apply.
why: Lets users inspect and selectively cherry-pick mixed agent proposals without premature side effects.
evidence: S14, D03; Budget A (price 120→125), B (heading), C (cost 70→72 unsupported)

statement: 'Review selected' calculates exact arithmetic and scoped changed-value counts specifically for the chosen unit subset (e.g., A gives 276,000 profit and 24 changed cells in Monthly!B8:M11; A+C gives 252,000 and 36 changed cells).
why: Shows exact downstream impact of the user's chosen subset before committing.
evidence: S14; Budget A vs A+C subset previews

statement: Apply validates all selected units atomically before writing any target, yet records separate per-unit Undo steps in order (e.g., A then B) so a single Undo reverts only the heading edit while keeping the accepted price change.
why: Combines atomic pre-write safety with granular per-unit reversibility.
evidence: S14, S15; undo B heading keeps A price 125 & R276,000 profit

statement: Change history records proposal authorship, human acceptance, rejection, and undone state with a copyable change record; rejecting an unsupported suggestion updates only the proposal record and leaves the workbook untouched.
why: Maintains an auditable trail of human-agent collaboration.
evidence: S14, S15; History panel & Copy change record

source: pro21/agent.html S16 (callout 5, UI), S14 (exception), S15 (exception), D03 (callout 2)
statement: When a cell changes after an agent proposal was created (expected 120, current 123, proposed 125), applying any selection containing the stale unit is blocked atomically so it never overwrites the newer value; users can Recompute a fresh preview against current values or deselect the conflicting unit to review independent units separately.
why: Prevents silent overwrites when workbooks evolve concurrently with agent proposals.

source: pro21/customise.html G01 (callouts 2, 4, UI, exception), G03 (callout 3), O02 (callout 4)
statement: Macro security levels are exactly Off, Guarded, and Unguarded, controlled solely by the host (never granted by a theme, App, or workbook layout); Off refuses all macro actions, protected cells block writes before execution, and Unguarded never manufactures a missing VBA runtime or external capability.
why: Establishes a crisp three-tier macro security model under strict host authority.

statement: Under Guarded mode, a macro with a declared workbook-write plan (`AppActions.StressRate` setting `Loan!B3 → 12%`) shows source text and declared actions for scoped per-run trust review, recalculates existing formulas on approval, and records one attributable workbook Undo step restoring prior values and dependents.
why: Makes simple workbook-mutating macros inspectable and reversible.

statement: An illustrative VBA views library (`Views.TryShow "Classic"`, `Views.SelectBlock "Loan", "B2:B6"`) lets macros request view switches and block selections while preserving shared workbook state; view/selection actions record as navigation without consuming a workbook Undo step or altering calculation mode, and fall back to native worksheet selection in Classic when the optional views library is unavailable.
why: Lets VBA macros coordinate cleanly with DNA Calc views while remaining Excel-compatible.

statement: When a declared action batch includes an unavailable external capability (e.g., `ExportQuote` writing `Loan!B3` then opening `quote.csv`), preflight rejects the complete batch before the first write so zero actions execute, `Loan!B3` stays unchanged, and no external side effect is ever portrayed as undoable.
why: Prevents partial workbook mutations before an unavailable external side effect fails.

source: pro21/customise.html G01 (callout 5), G02 (callout 5), G03 (callout 4); verification.html §What was checked list 2
statement: Pro 21 explicitly warns that finite declared local action plans demonstrate a trust and review interface, NOT proof that a production host can preflight, sandbox, or roll back arbitrary VBA, and the proposed views-library API spelling is illustrative.
why: Avoids over-promising static preflight or rollback guarantees for arbitrary legacy VBA.

statement: Verification of the 25,000-row Sales fixture independently reconstructs expected counts, sums, and regional ranks from the row specification in a separate loop rather than calling production code to build expectations, checking exact integer amounts across Pending, Paid, All, and partial date windows.
why: Eliminates circular self-verification bugs in test fixtures.
evidence: README.md, verification.html; Pending days 1–14 = 2,073 rows / R2,334,750

statement: Verification reporting keeps heterogeneous units separate — assertions, scenario groups, focused checks, thumbnail targets, and static visual proofs — rather than summing them into one inflated test total.
why: Prevents inflated metrics and keeps QA evidence auditable.

statement: Five cast workbooks (Budget, Sales, Loan, Stock, Inherited) plus workbook-free Formula Explorer supply concrete shared arithmetic checkpoints across all views, keeping full calculation precision strictly separate from display rounding.
why: Grounds design reviews in realistic, checkable numerical fixtures instead of dummy text.

statement: Cross-module experience checks verify: synchronized M02/I03 clock tick counters/breadcrumbs/reset boundaries; File re-entry preserving workbook/sheet/filename and accepted customisation; scoped New-from-pattern Undo; Explorer aligning metadata/tree/result and Ctrl+Enter/Evaluate Undo; and first-viewport 1440×900 composition fit without clipping primary actions.
why: Captures multi-view integration invariants that must hold in the production application.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 1, 6; verification.html §What was checked ¶3 & list 6
statement: Prototype validation used jsdom and offline WeasyPrint proofs without native browser access; native rendering, platform font metrics, real event delivery, OS shortcut interception, screen-reader behaviour, and WCAG conformance remain uncertified.
why: Clarifies what requires real browser and assistive-technology testing in implementation.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 2; verification.html §What was checked list 1; W05 (callout 3); NC01–NC07 (last callout)
statement: No native XLSX/XLSM writer, real Excel evaluation, custom-XML preservation, unknown-part retention, or macro-project preservation was tested; the prototype checks only local fixture evaluation and JSON serialization of view declarations.
why: Separates design-contract fidelity from tested Excel file round-trip compatibility.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 2, 3; verification.html §What was checked list 2
statement: No real VBA engine, native XLL/XLAM binary, COM RTD provider, or external network feed executed; all add-in, RTD, and macro behaviours are bounded JavaScript fixture simulations.
why: Prevents prototype interaction checks from being mistaken for native host runtime verification.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 4; verification.html §What was checked list 3
statement: Formula Explorer's per-function Excel call-match counts and worst-ULP figures (e.g., GAMMA 4,252/4,311 · 63 ulp) are labelled sample archive records illustrating UI presentation, not live corpus measurements.
why: Prevents illustrative UI figures from being cited as measured engine parity.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 5; verification.html §What was checked list 4; W01 (callout 3); M03–M05 (callout 1)
statement: Inherited's 40 sheets, 300,000 formula members, 6 hidden sheets, 90 directed links, and 85,272 reference records come from a deterministic manifest fixture rather than a native workbook scan or timed performance benchmark.
why: Distinguishes scale-UX manifest testing from real engine performance benchmarking.

source: pro21/README.md §What remains unverified list 6; verification.html §What was checked list 5; O03 (callout 4)
statement: Native OS print dialogs, browser pagination, physical/PDF print output, OS clipboard permissions, and download prompts were not certified.
why: Marks OS-level shell integrations that require native desktop/browser verification.

statement: Pro 21 cites 16 primary Microsoft documentation references (T1–T16: RTD/IRTDUpdateEvent/IRtdServer/ThrottleInterval, Calculation/MaxIterations/calcPr/Recalculation/AfterCalculate, FILTER, GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, LAMBDA, Dynamic arrays, LET, Defined Names) as design-contract grounding without claiming native execution certification.
why: Anchors proposed workbook mappings and push-backs in primary Excel documentation.

source: pro21/README.md §Files table, §Other new scenes; verification.html §Package contents, §All 73 scenes
statement: Pro 21 retains all 43 Pro 20 scenes and adds 30 new scenes (NC01–NC07, W01–W05, U01–U05, O01–O04, M03–M05, G01–G03, E01–E03) for 73 unique scenes across 13 HTML files plus verification.html and README.md (78 gallery thumbnail targets where 5 Explorer/Agent storyboard moments also appear in specialist collections).
why: Defines the complete scene inventory superseding Pro 20 without dropping any original scene.
evidence: README.md, verification.html; 73 unique scenes, 15 ZIP members

source: pro21/verification.html §Coverage of the round-three brief table
statement: Pro 21 maps every round-three brief requirement (A1–A8 computation notebook and B1–B8 patterns, mixed views, customisation, file/print, scale map, Guarded macros, Formula Explorer, and cross-view/clock fixes) to interactive normal/exception scenes, defining 'finished' strictly as prototype interaction and check coverage.
why: Tracks full requirement coverage while keeping prototype vs production boundaries explicit.
